blocks.content: In-situ Conservation – protecting species within their natural habitat.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: In-situ conservation focuses on protecting species directly within their natural ecosystems.
In-situ methods include National Parks, Wildlife Sanctuaries, Biosphere Reserves, and Community Reserves.
Ex-situ conservation involves off-site protection of species outside their natural habitats.
Ex-situ techniques utilize facilities such as Zoos, Botanical Gardens, Seed Banks, Gene Banks, and Cryopreservation.

blocks.content: Ex-situ Conservation – conservation outside natural habitat.

items: Competitive exams frequently ask to classify specific methods like Cryopreservation or Seed Banks as either In-situ or Ex-situ.
Remember that National Parks and Biosphere Reserves preserve the natural habitat (In-situ), whereas Botanical Gardens and Gene Banks conserve species in artificial/off-site settings (Ex-situ).
